title: Run Nerva as a coding agent inside an editor (ACP)
contract: `hermes acp` runs an ACP JSON-RPC agent over stdio so Zed / VS Code / JetBrains drive Hermes as their coding agent: initialize advertising load_session + fork/list/resume + image prompts; session new/load/resume/fork/list (cursor, 50/page)/cancel/prompt; workspace cwd binding with Windows→WSL path translation; sessions persisted into state.db with source="acp"; a dedicated 29-tool `hermes-acp` toolset with no messaging/audio/clarify; a benign liveness-probe log filter; shipped as the `[acp]` extra with three invocation spellings and a `--check` preflight. Inventory ids acp-mcp-dev.hermes-acp, .acp-initialize, .acp-authenticate, .acp-session-new/-load/-resume/-fork/-list/-cancel, .acp-prompt, .acp-cwd, .acp-session-persistence, .acp-toolset, .acp-probe-filter, .acp-packaging (acp_adapter/entry.py, acp_adapter/server.py, acp_adapter/session.py).
governance: The transport is read-only, but every tool reached through it performs effects. The ACP session must call the same orchestrator path so file.write, terminal.exec, browser.step and desktop.step still cross kernel.authorize; an ACP-local tool loop that talks to drivers directly would be the regression.

- Windows to WSL path translation
- a dedicated editor toolset (turns use the agent's normal tool profile)
- liveness-probe log filter

- not verified against a live Zed/JetBrains build or a live hub turn (fake backend in tests)

title: Approve a dangerous command or a file edit from inside the editor, with the real diff shown first
contract: Two bridges. `acp_adapter/permissions.py` turns Hermes' blocking approval prompt into an ACP `session/request_permission` with allow_once / allow_session / allow_always / deny / deny_always, probing the installed SDK for optional option kinds, mapping answers back to Hermes' vocabulary, and returning a distinct `"timeout"` verdict after 60 s. `acp_adapter/edit_approval.py` computes the *post-edit* text before the tool runs (write_file, patch replace-mode via fuzzy_find_and_replace, V4A patch bodies), shows it as an `acp.tool_diff_content` diff, fails closed on any requester error, and applies a three-mode auto-approve policy (ask / workspace_session / session) with `.git`, `.ssh`, `.env*`, `id_rsa`, `id_ed25519` always asking. Session modes default/accept_edits/dont_ask plus `session/set_mode` and `session/set_config_option` expose that policy to the editor (acp-mcp-dev.acp-permission-bridge, .acp-edit-approval, .acp-session-modes, .acp-set-session-mode, .acp-set-config-option).
governance: This IS the governance surface. It must render kernel/approval-queue decisions, never replace them: an editor 'allow always' maps to a permission-ledger grant crossing permission.grant, not to a local bypass flag.
remaining_verbatim:
- per-session edit auto-approve modes and session/set_mode / set_config_option: deliberately not built, an editor cannot widen Nerva's approval mode (the owner's global /approvals dial still applies)
- V4A/patch-style edit previews (Nerva has file_write/file_delete only)
- not verified against a live editor

title: Steer, inspect and control a running editor thread (in-thread commands + live rendering)
contract: Nine commands advertised as data so the editor autocompletes them (`available_commands_update`) and dispatched before the text reaches the model, each running in a fresh contextvars context pinned to the session cwd: /help /model /tools /context /reset /compress /steer /queue /version; unknown `/words` fall through to the model as prose. Alongside them the whole rendering layer: tool calls mapped to ACP kinds with bespoke per-tool titles and file locations plus ~20 per-tool result formatters and a `_POLISHED_TOOLS` raw-output suppression set; a FIFO queue of call ids per tool name so parallel calls attach to the right card; the `todo` tool projected into Zed's native plan panel; token/usage updates including cached-read tokens; `_meta.hermes.sessionProvenance` exposing compaction lineage; compaction-summary markers; and full transcript replay awaited inside session/load (acp-mcp-dev.acp-available-commands, .acp-slash-dispatch, .acp-cmd-*, .acp-set-session-model, .acp-model-state, .acp-tool-rendering, .acp-toolcall-fifo, .acp-plan-updates, .acp-usage-update, .acp-provenance, .acp-compaction-meta, .acp-history-replay).
governance: read-only — projection and display only. /compress and /model rebuild agent state and must stay session-scoped; /steer writes into a running turn and inherits that turn's existing authorization.

- usage updates, provenance/compaction _meta, transcript replay on session/load
- /model, /steer, /queue have no hub command equivalent to advertise
- not verified against a live editor

title: Let the editor hand the agent MCP servers that exist only for that session
contract: `session/new|load|resume|fork` accept an `mcpServers` array; each is registered off-loop via asyncio.to_thread and expands the session's toolsets with one `mcp-<name>` toolset per server on top of `hermes-acp`. A bounded join (`mcp_discovery_timeout`, default 1.5 s) means a dead server cannot block session creation, and a scheduled late refresh re-reads the registry after discovery finishes because the agent snapshots tools once at build time (acp-mcp-dev.acp-session-mcp).
governance: read-only to register, but the tools it registers perform effects and must land behind the same outbound MCP authorization gate as any other server (see the outbound-MCP row); a per-session server must not inherit a wider trust tier than a configured one.
remaining_verbatim:
- session/load, resume and fork (not offered) cannot carry mcpServers
- the route waits up to 15 s for a first connect (Hermes 1.5 s off-loop join); a slow server joins at a later turn
- not verified against a live editor

title: Use a third-party agent CLI (GitHub Copilot) as a model backend over ACP
contract: `agent/copilot_acp_client.py` drives `copilot --acp --stdio` as an OpenAI-shaped chat backend: `--help` probe cached per binary before spawn, credentials-inheriting-but-Tier-1-stripped subprocess env, a full JSON-RPC dance, permissions auto-denied (no human channel), and an fs bridge confined to the session cwd with read redaction and fail-closed writes. `agent/acp_openai_bridge.py` carries OpenAI tool schemas into the prompt as text and regex-extracts `<tool_call>` blocks back out, with an allowlist so an autonomous CLI is not re-offered overlapping tools (acp-mcp-dev.copilot-acp-client, .acp-openai-bridge).
governance: would be a governance hole by construction — the foreign process performs file reads/writes through its own bridge, never crossing kernel.authorize.
historical_exclusion_reason: This makes Nerva a shell around somebody else's agent, which inverts the product: the whole claim is that Nerva mediates actions, and a foreign CLI that owns its own loop and auto-denies its own permission prompts is precisely the thing the kernel cannot see inside. Prompt-carried tool schemas parsed back out by regex is also a fragile contract to inherit. Re-open if a specific local agent CLI becomes a model Nerva needs and can be run tool-less, as a pure text completion backend with no fs bridge.

title: Show the agent the semantic errors its own edit just introduced
contract: Real language servers as background subprocesses feeding an `lsp_diagnostics` field on every successful write_file/patch: baseline the file's current diagnostics, write, re-query, subtract, report only what is new — with a freshness gate so a diagnostic counts only if the server produced it for the post-edit content, and `range_shift.py` re-anchoring baseline ranges across the edit. A 27-server registry with extension-or-basename matching and a language-id map decoupled from it; 14 install recipes across npm/go/pip plus an explicit manual tier, staged into a Hermes-owned directory that never touches a shared prefix; `hermes lsp status|list|install|install-all|restart|which` including a backend warning for the 'spawns fine but silently emits nothing' case; lazy spawn, idle reaping with a clamped timeout, a broken-pair set, and silent fallback to the syntax-only result on any failure (acp-mcp-dev.lsp-diagnostics, .lsp-root, .lsp-status, .lsp-list, .lsp-install, .lsp-install-all, .lsp-restart, .lsp-which, .lsp-registry, .lsp-install-recipes, .lsp-config, .lsp-service).
governance: read-only, but it auto-installs binaries from npm/go/pip onto the owner's machine, which would need the lazy-deps allowlist posture and a kernel hop before any install.
remaining_verbatim:
- diagnostics only on file_write (Nerva has no separate patch tool)
- a trusted workspace can still steer some servers into running its code inside the sandbox (a pyrightconfig.json venv's Python; each server's own config files): see profiles.py
- no sandboxed path where bwrap is unavailable (macOS/Windows): servers there need the owner's explicit opt-out
- live acceptance beyond pyright and typescript-language-server (both exercised by hand under bwrap; the suite uses a fake server)
